# Alyx

{{ site_header }} - a database of experimental neuroscience metadata, served at {{ base_url }}.

> If you are an automated client retrieving more than a page or two of records, use the ONE
> API rather than this REST interface. ONE downloads cache tables and queries them locally, so
> a search costs no database queries. Paging this API for bulk data is slow, heavily rate
> limited, and loads a database other people are using. This is not a formality: naive clients
> paging large endpoints have taken this database down.

## Preferred access: ONE

- Documentation: https://int-brain-lab.github.io/ONE/
- Source and MCP server: https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ONE ; https://int-brain-lab.gitmcp.io/ONE

```python
from one.api import ONE
one = ONE(base_url='{{ base_url }}')
eids = one.search(subject='example', date_range=['2024-01-01', '2024-12-31'])
```

`search`, `list_datasets` and `load_dataset` read the local cache tables. Use `mode='remote'`
only when you need something the cache does not hold, such as a live QC value.

ONE asks for a credential the first time and remembers it: pass `username='<username>'` for an
account with a password, or `token='<token>'` for one without. Later sessions need neither.

## REST API, when you genuinely need it

- Interactive documentation: {{ base_url }}/docs/
- Machine-readable schema: {{ base_url }}/api/schema
- Endpoint index: {{ base_url }}/api/

Authentication is required on every endpoint:

    Authorization: Token <key>

Obtain a key from {{ base_url }}/me, or by POSTing a username and password to
{{ base_url }}/auth-token. Sending the header to {{ base_url }}/me returns the account the key
belongs to - the cheapest way to check a key, and the only way to learn who it speaks for.

### Limits

- Page size is capped at {{ max_limit }} records. A larger `?limit=` is silently reduced; the
  response says so in its `detail` field.
- Requests are rate limited. A 429 carries `Retry-After`; respect it rather than retrying
  immediately.
- If a query matches thousands of records, that is the signal to switch to ONE, not to write a
  loop over `next`.
